title: Observability data access fencing & differential retention playground
creator: Aisha Khan
description:
Goal: Build a small, low-risk playground that proves the end-to-end pattern for tenant-scoped access fencing and differential retention on observability streams (traces, logs, metrics) without regressing latency dashboards or error signal fidelity.

Scope:
- Tracing hooks: add a lightweight span annotation (sensitivity_level) at service SDKs to mark PII-containing spans or high-risk requests.
- Pipeline transforms: implement streaming transformers in the telemetry ingest pipeline to apply masks, tokenization, or field dropping based on sensitivity_level and tenant policy.
- Retention policy engine: prototype a policy evaluator that maps tenant risk & label -> retention window (e.g., 7d/30d/90d) and archival tier.
- RBAC and access logging: enforce role-scoped read access to raw vs redacted observability streams and emit immutable access audit events.
- Dashboards: ensure latency/error dashboards consume redacted aggregates or masked traces while preserving alerting thresholds.

Non-goals for this ticket (out of scope): full multi-region rollout, advanced pseudonymization, billing integration.

Design notes and trade-offs:
- Masking vs dropping: masking fields keeps shape for parsers and reduces downstream schema churn at cost of potential re-identification risks; dropping guarantees no data but may break percentile buckets. We'll default to deterministic masking for known PII fields and configurable dropping for freeform payloads.
- Sampling: to keep storage/ingest costs bounded, differential retention must pair with sampling tiers. We will prototype a two-tier sampler: high-fidelity (100%) for 7d then sampled rolloff to 1% for older tiers.
- Latency: the stream transformers will be implemented as async, CPU-light operations in the ingest tier to avoid adding p95 latency >10ms. If profiling shows higher impact, we'll move heavy transforms to async archival path and provide a short-lived raw cache for recent queries.
- RBAC enforcement point: implement gates at the query layer (Console/API) rather than at storage for easier rollback. All accesses to raw partitions will require a short-lived decryption token and be logged.

Acceptance criteria:
1) Telemetry SDK emits the new sensitivity_level span tag and a feature-flagged tracer shim is available in the mono-repo.
2) Ingest pipeline can apply masking rules for at least three field types (email, uuid, freeform text) with unit + integration tests.
3) Policy engine returns retention windows for tenants and the ingest pipeline honors those windows for new data writes.
4) Console query respects RBAC for raw vs redacted streams; queries for raw data require an audit event and elevated role.
5) End-to-end tests show latency dashboard aggregates (p50/p95/p99) remain within 2% of baseline when using masked streams.
6) Documentation (Confluence) and a short runbook for operator troubleshooting are published.

Rollout plan:
- Week 1: SDK tracer shim + unit tests (dev cluster).
- Week 2: Transformer prototype + policy engine POC (dev -> staging).
- Week 3: Integrate RBAC checks into Console query layer and add access-logging.
- Week 4: Internal canary using two internal tenants, monitor SLOs; iterate.
- Week 5: Beta canary with 3 non-production customers and security review signoff.

Monitoring & success metrics:
- Ingest p95 latency change (target < +10ms).
- Percentage of sensitive fields successfully masked (target >= 99% for synthetic test set).
- Number of raw-data access events per week (audit signal).
- Dashboard fidelity: alerts fired pre/post masking remain stable (<=2% false positives).

Implementation risks & mitigations:
- Risk: Missing or inconsistent telemetry field names from producers. Mitigation: provide lightweight SDK adapter and transformer rules that map known producers; fallback to freeform scanning for untagged events at lower priority.
- Risk: KMS availability for short-lived decryption tokens. Mitigation: cache tokens in HSM-backed gateway with fail-open limited to redacted queries only (requires security signoff).

Next steps & deliverables:
- Create PR for telemetry SDK shim and link it here.
- Deliver transformer module + test harness.
- Draft policy engine API and sample tenant policy file.

Notes: this playground is expected to produce a clear ops pattern we can reuse when we migrate the larger telemetry fleet to tenant-aware retention and access controls.
